neighbours.label: ' has' inside a relative clause on a superlative or quantified head ('the best that the city [has] to offer', 'the patience she [has] shown'); main-clause ' has' is silent
fire: The brochure lists the best that the island has to offer families.
The tour samples everything the old quarter has to offer.
Be grateful for the kindness she has shown your children.
The market sells the finest produce the county has to offer.
He wasted the trust his teacher has placed in him.
We enjoyed all that the coast has to offer in spring.
Remember the many chances life has given you so far.
It is the warmest welcome the town has ever given a visitor.
quiet: The island has three beaches and a ferry for families.
The old quarter has narrow streets and a busy square.
She has shown your children how to bake bread.
The county has a market every Friday in summer.
His teacher has placed the books on the top shelf.
The coast has mild weather in spring.
Life has changed a great deal in ten years.
The town has welcomed a visitor from Japan.

notes: Card flags the pole broad (1.2% of tokens reach 0.1 of max), so this is a best guess at one driver, not the whole pole. Probes: 0.15-0.33 on relative-clause ' has', 0.02-0.03 on main-clause ' has'; other card contexts (' our', ' of', ' way') reach similar levels.
